newsitem.title: ITALY: Former anti-Mafia chief denies graft charges.
newsitem.headline: Former anti-Mafia chief denies graft charges.

text.p: The former head of Italy's anti-Mafia police, who resigned after prosecutors began investigating him for alleged corruption, pleaded his innocence in an Italian newspaper interview on Thursday.

General Giovanni Verdicchio, who quit on Saturday, told La Repubblica that a payment of 20 million lire ($10,800) he received from a Rome businessman was not a kickback but money from a legitimate share dealing.
"I would have had to be a real fool to take 20 million lire and leave such obvious traces," he said.
"I am bitter and humiliated. I ask myself who will give me back my respectability, my honour. But that's how things go in Italian justice."

Verdicchio is under investigation in the central Italian city of Perugia on suspicion of having received kickbacks from businessmen while he headed the main unit of Italy's fiscal police in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
He is expected to be questioned in the next few days.
The Interior Ministry said it would soon name a new director for the anti-Mafia unit, which runs investigations into the mob by all Italian police forces.
